verdict.rationale: Spline documents its own no-code interactivity model built from states, events and actions. Webhooks and the Real-time API let a project automatically trigger actions and respond to events, and the Events system can fire Scene Transition actions. The evidence is only short first-party snippets, so the depth of rule-definition isn't shown. missing for 10: documented catalogue of event types and action types, conditional or rule logic (if/then filters on events), evidence that AI agents or MCP can author these rules, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Most interactivity in Spline needs no code at all. It's built from **states, events and actions**
By using webhooks, your Spline project can automatically trigger actions, update variables, and react to data sent from external sources
The Real-time API feature in Spline allows you to integrate external services, retrieve or send data, and automate responses based on events.
It's possible to transition between scenes with the Events system by using a Scene Transition action.
